questions.q: In this lab's agent, what role does Cortex Search play versus Cortex Analyst?
options: Cortex Search handles unstructured documents (guides, incident write-ups); Cortex Analyst handles structured tables via natural-language-to-SQL
They do the exact same job and are interchangeable
Cortex Search only works on numeric data; Cortex Analyst only works on text
Cortex Analyst indexes documents; Cortex Search queries tables
questions.explain: Cortex Search is for semantic search over unstructured content; Cortex Analyst translates natural language into SQL against structured tables — the agent combines both and picks per question.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend checking the AI Readiness Score before building the agent's tools?
options: Low semantic view coverage signals you should build a proper Semantic View first, rather than pointing Cortex Analyst at raw, undocumented tables
The AI Readiness Score is required by Snowflake before any Cortex Agent can be created
It replaces the need for a Cortex Search service entirely
It automatically fixes masking policies on the underlying tables
questions.explain: A low score on the tables you're about to expose is a signal to invest in a real Semantic View first, matching Lesson 71's guidance.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend wiring governance in alongside the agent's tools, rather than adding it after the agent already works?
options: So Agent Identity, masking/row access, guardrails, and approval gates are in place before real users or real data show up, not retrofitted under pressure later
Because Snowflake technically prevents adding governance after an agent is created
Because governance controls make the agent's tools run faster
Because evaluation metrics can only be computed if governance is configured first
questions.explain: The lesson frames governance-from-day-one as the practical difference between a demo and a production-ready agent — not a technical requirement, but a design discipline.

questions.q: What does a low tool_selection_accuracy score specifically indicate about an agent, according to this lesson?
options: The agent is reaching for the wrong tool for a given question — an architecture problem that prompt tuning on the final answer won't fix
The agent's warehouse is undersized
The underlying Semantic View has a syntax error
The agent's masking policy is misconfigured
questions.explain: tool_selection_accuracy specifically measures whether the orchestration layer calls the expected tools — a low score points to a tool-selection/architecture issue, not an answer-wording issue.

questions.q: This course's closing lesson lists an eight-item production-readiness checklist. Which of these pairs correctly matches a checklist item to the lesson it came from?
options: Masking/row access policies reacting to IS_AGENT_ACTIVATED — from Lesson 75
AI Readiness Score — from Lesson 73 (Agent Identity)
AI Guardrails — from Lesson 69 (Evaluations)
Approval gate on state-modifying actions — from Lesson 70 (Horizon Catalog)
questions.explain: Lesson 75 covered writing masking and row access policies keyed off IS_AGENT_ACTIVATED; the other options in this question mismatch their checklist item to the wrong lesson.
